function.name: calculate_electric_field

charge.description: Charge in coulombs producing the electric field. This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Proteins that are commonly found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|-------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; serve as channels, transporters, receptors, or anchors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (facilitated diffusion)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., β‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin
• **Ionotropic glutamate receptors** (ligand‑gated ion channels)
• **Connexin 43** (gap‑junction hemichannel)
• **Integrins** (cell‑matrix adhesion)
• **Cadherins** (cell‑cell adhesion)
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** – e.g., EGFR, HER2 | | **Peripheral membrane proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface via electrostatic or lipid‑anchoring interactions; often link to the cytoskeleton or signaling complexes. | • **Ankyrin‑B** (links integral proteins to spectrin)
• **Spectrin** (cytoskeletal scaffold)
• **Actin** (sub‑membrane cortical network)
• **Src family kinases** (membrane‑associated signaling)
• **GAP-43** (neuronal growth factor)
• **Moesin** (ERM family, links actin to membrane proteins) | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to lipids (e.g., GPI anchors) and reside on the outer leaflet. | • **CD59** (protectin, GPI‑anchored)
• **Prion protein (PrP^C)** (GPI‑anchored)
• **Receptor for activated C‑kinase 1 (RACK1)** (GPI‑anchored) | | **Extracellular matrix‑binding proteins** | Interact with the extracellular matrix and help anchor the cell. | • **Fibronectin** (secreted, binds integrins)
• **Collagen type IV** (basement membrane component) | ### How to use this list - **Research**: If you’re studying a particular signaling pathway, look for the relevant GPCRs or receptor tyrosine kinases in the table. - **Biochemistry**: When purifying membrane fractions, you can target these proteins with specific antibodies or affinity tags. - **Cell biology**: Understanding the interplay between integral and peripheral proteins helps explain membrane dynamics, cell adhesion, and signal transduction. Feel free to ask for more details on any specific protein family or for a deeper dive into their structure‑function relationships!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?" They want a list of proteins found in the plasma membrane. We can provide a general answer: types of proteins: integral membrane proteins (e.g., ion channels, transporters, receptors), peripheral membrane proteins (e.g., cytoskeletal proteins, signaling proteins). Provide examples: e.g., Na+/K+ ATPase, GLUT1, G-protein coupled receptors, integrins, cadherins, connexins, etc. Also mention peripheral proteins like actin-binding proteins, ankyrin, spectrin. Provide a concise but informative answer. No function calls needed.
